profiles.name: Joe Stern
profiles.description: Joe Stern was cited for contempt after refusing to answer questions before the Ohio Un-American Activities Commission. A state court convicted him and imposed ten days in jail and a $500 fine. When the consolidated cases reached the U.S. Supreme Court in 1959, the Court reversed the judgments against Richard Raley, Alice Brown, and Irving Morgan. Stern’s judgment was affirmed by an equally divided Court because Justice Potter Stewart did not participate. Available court records do not establish whether Stern served the ten-day jail term.

profiles.name: Joseph Cort
profiles.description: Joseph Cort was a Massachusetts-born physician and research physiologist who had belonged to the Communist Party while at Yale. He left the United States for Britain in 1951 and remained abroad after receiving draft orders. A federal grand jury indicted him for draft evasion in 1954 after he had moved to Czechoslovakia. Because he was outside the United States, the indictment did not result in American arrest or confinement. The Supreme Court later protected his right to challenge the government’s attempt to strip his citizenship.

The prosecution was later abandoned after the Supreme Court invalidated state sedition prosecutions preempted by federal law.
